description: Liberation or release from the cycle of transmigration; both ਮੁਕਤਿ (Sanskrit mukti) and ਮੋਖ/ਮੋਖੁ (Sanskrit moksha) are used interchangeably; the highest aspiration is ਜੀਵਨ ਮੁਕਤਿ — liberation while still living.
caveats: None specific; both roots are unambiguous in SGGS usage.

description: The cycle of birth (ਜਨਮ) and death (ਮਰਣ/ਮਰਨ), the fundamental existential condition from which mukti is sought; escape from this cycle is the central soteriological goal in Gurbani.
caveats: ਮਰਿ (204 hits) is highly polysemous — 'dying-while-alive' (positive spiritual death of ego) as well as physical death; must be disambiguated by context. ਜਨਮ alone can also mean simply 'birth' in a non-cyclical sense.

description: The round of reincarnation — coming and going (ਆਵਣ ਜਾਵਣ / ਆਵਣ ਜਾਣ) — expressed in Gurbani as a phrase rather than the single Sanskrit compound ਆਵਾਗਵਣ (which does not appear as one token in the corpus); cessation of this cycle is mukti.
caveats: The compound word ਆਵਾਗਵਣ does NOT appear as a single token in word_freq; Gurbani uses the split phrase ਆਵਣ ਜਾਵਣ/ਜਾਣ. ਆਵੈ (535 hits) and ਜਾਇ (1012 hits) are extremely common general verbs; only instances clearly referring to repeated births/deaths should be counted for the concept. Terms such as ਆਵਾ (39 hits) may sometimes carry the sense of the whole world of coming-and-going.

description: Yama / the death-messenger (ਜਮ); also ਜਮਕਾਲ (Yama the time-death), ਜਮਕੰਕਰ (Yama's agents), ਜਮਦੂਤ (messengers of death), and ਜਮਪੁਰਿ (the city of Yama); Nam-simran is the recurring remedy against Jam's reach.
caveats: ਜਮੁਨ/ਜਮੁਨਾ (Yamuna river, 9 hits combined) is a false friend; ਜਮਾਇਆ/ਜਮਾਵੈ etc. are verbal forms of 'to gather/assemble' — unrelated.

description: The terrifying world-ocean (ਭਵਜਲੁ / ਭਉਜਲੁ — both spellings co-exist) of existential existence through which the soul must cross; ਦੁਤਰੁ ('difficult to cross') is used as a near-synonym adjective; the Guru's Word (Shabad) is the boat.
caveats: ਭਵਜਲੁ and ਭਉਜਲੁ are the same concept; the ਭਉ- spelling foregrounds the 'fear' root while ਭਵ- foregrounds 'existence/becoming' — both appear freely in the corpus. ਭਵ (66 hits) alone means 'existence/world' but is not exclusively the ocean metaphor.

description: The phenomenal world (ਸੰਸਾਰੁ, ਜਗਤੁ, ਜਗੁ, ਦੁਨੀਆ) understood in Gurbani as transient, illusion-laden, and governed by Maya; the world is not condemned but is seen as the arena where devotion either binds or liberates.
caveats: ਮਾਇਆ (824 hits) is the dominant 'world-as-illusion' term but conceptually overlaps with both ਸੰਸਾਰ and ਗਰਬ/ਹਉਮੈ clusters — include with annotation. ਲੋਕ can mean 'people' as well as 'world/realm'. ਜਗਿ is the locative case 'in the world' — not a lemma distinct from ਜਗੁ.

description: Devotion (ਭਗਤਿ) to the Divine — the path and practice of loving surrender; also ਭਗਤ/ਭਗਤਾ referring to the devotee or saint; Gurbani affirms that bhagti without Nam is incomplete (ਭਗਤਿਹੀਣੁ = devoid of devotion is a reproach).
caveats: ਭਗਤ (262 hits) serves double duty as noun ('a devotee / saint') and as the root of ਭਗਤਿ (devotion) — context distinguishes. Compare closely with ਸੰਤ/ਸਾਧ cluster.

description: Divine love in its various registers — ਪ੍ਰੇਮ/ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ (spiritual love/longing), ਪਿਆਰ (affection), ਪਿਰ/ਪਿਰੁ (the Beloved Lord cast in the bride-groom metaphor), and ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ (the Beloved); the soul-bride's longing for the Divine Husband is a central Gurbani trope.
caveats: ਮੋਹ/ਮੋਹੁ/ਮੋਹਿ (782 combined hits, NOT included in total) is a significant false friend: it primarily means worldly attachment/infatuation — a spiritual obstacle, not divine love. Only in rare contexts does ਮੋਹਿ carry devotional longing. ਪਿਆਰੇ (332) is frequently a vocative form of address ('O Beloved') and may not always indicate the abstract concept.

description: The reverential Fear of God (ਭਉ/ਭੈ) — not terror but awe-infused surrender; paired with ਭਾਉ (divine love/devotion) in the classic Gurbani couplet ਭੈ ਭਾਉ; the Divine itself is ਨਿਰਭਉ (without fear/feud) — the Mool Mantar attribute; ਭਉਜਲੁ (ocean-of-fear/existence) is a compound form.
caveats: ਭੈ (300 hits) is polysemous: it means both reverential divine fear (positive, path to liberation) and mundane fear/terror (negative). Disambiguation requires line context. ਭਾਉ (193 hits) overlaps with the prem_pyar cluster — 'loving devotion' is a meaning shared between them. ਨਿਰਭਉ in the Mool Mantar is an attribute of God, not a human state.

description: Divine grace in multiple registers: ਕਿਰਪਾ (grace/mercy, most frequent), ਨਦਰਿ/ਨਦਰੀ (the Glance of Grace — Guru's transforming look), ਦਇਆ/ਦਇਆਲ (compassion/the Compassionate), ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ (by Grace/blessing, Gur Prasaad in Mool Mantar), ਮਿਹਰ/ਮਿਹਰਵਾਨ (Persian: mercy/the Merciful); grace and personal effort (karam as deed) are both present — Gurbani holds the Glance of Grace (nadar) as the final gateway.
caveats: CRITICAL FALSE FRIEND: ਕਰਮ/ਕਰਮੁ/ਕਰਮਿ (635 combined hits) is radically ambiguous — (a) Persian karam = grace/blessing (as in 'ਕਰਮੀ ਆਵੈ ਕਪੜਾ ਨਦਰੀ ਮੋਖੁ ਦੁਆਰੁ' where ਕਰਮੀ = by Grace); (b) Sanskrit karma = deeds/actions/fate from past lives. The two meanings cannot be separated by word-form alone; line-level context is mandatory. ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ in the formula 'ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ' is specifically 'by the Guru's Grace' — a structurally important token.

description: Eternal Truth as both Divine Name (ਸਚੁ = the True One) and the quality of authenticity/truthfulness; ਸਚਿਆਰੁ/ਸਚਿਆਰਾ = the truth-attuned person; ਸਤਿ as in 'ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ' (the Name is Truth) in the Mool Mantar; ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ = the True Guru.
caveats: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ/ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ/ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ (2013 combined hits) refer to the True Guru as a person/institution, not to the abstract Truth concept alone — include with clear annotation. ਸਤਿ (252 hits) in isolation can mean Truth but very frequently appears as a prefix in ਸਤਿਗੁਰ, ਸਤਿਨਾਮੁ etc.; standalone ਸਤਿ hits require context check. ਸਚ ਖੰਡਿ (Realm of Truth, Japji) is a two-token phrase — ਖੰਡ (79 hits) is not exclusively this compound.

description: The saint or holy person (ਸੰਤ/ਸਾਧ/ਸਾਧੂ) and the company of saints (ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ/ਸੰਗਤਿ = the congregation/holy assembly); Gurbani holds the ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ as the primary transformative environment — the dust of the saint's feet is a recurring image of liberation.
caveats: ਸੰਤਹੁ (93 hits) is the vocative plural 'O Saints!' — an address form, not a reference to a third person. ਸਾਧੂ and ਸਾਧ are used interchangeably; context distinguishes descriptive from vocative use. ਸੰਗਤਿ alone (185 hits) can mean any assembly — only reliably maps to the concept when paired with ਸਾਧ/ਸੰਤ context.

description: The spiritual path or way (ਮਾਰਗੁ, ਪੰਥੁ, ਰਾਹੁ, ਮਗੁ — all synonyms for 'road/path'); in Gurbani, the Guru shows the path (ਮਾਰਗਿ ਚਲਾਏ) and the devotee walks it; the concept emphasizes active wayfaring toward the Divine rather than a fixed sectarian path.
caveats: ਪੰਥ (4 hits) can also refer specifically to the Sikh Panth (community/tradition) — a sectarian meaning — distinct from the generic spiritual-path sense; context-dependent. ਮਗਿ is the locative 'on the path' — not distinct from ਮਗੁ lemma.

description: The divine Light (ਜੋਤਿ) that pervades all creation and inheres within every being; Gurbani's most recurring mystical image — the individual soul-flame is identical with the Divine Light; ਦੀਪਕੁ/ਦੀਵਾ (lamp) and ਨੂਰ (Persian: Light) are variant metaphors.
caveats: ਜੋਤਿ (310 hits) is predominantly the divine/inner Light concept; rarely refers to a literal flame. ਨੂਰ/ਨੂਰੁ (Persian, 6 hits) is rare and primarily in Bhagat Farid and Kabir compositions.

description: The unstruck celestial sound (ਅਨਹਦ/ਅਨਹਤ — both spellings) that reverberates within; ਨਾਦ (primordial sound), ਧੁਨਿ (resonance), ਝੁਣਕਾਰੁ (the ringing tone); ਸੁਰਤਿ (consciousness/attention) is the faculty that tunes in; ਸਬਦੁ/ਸਬਦਿ (the Shabad / Gurbani) is the manifest form of anhad heard through the Guru.
caveats: ਸਬਦੁ/ਸਬਦਿ (1659 combined hits) is the single most important Gurbani concept in this cluster but is a vast topic in its own right — it overlaps with anhad but also carries meaning of the Guru's teaching/word/scripture broadly. Include with annotation that Shabad concept merits its own entry. ਅਨਹਤ and ਅਨਹਦ are orthographic variants of the same Sanskrit anahat.

description: The purifier of the fallen/sinful (ਪਤਿਤ ਪਾਵਨ); in Gurbani ਪਤਿਤ ('the fallen/degraded') co-occurs with the Divine's capacity to uplift the most wretched — a key aspect of divine grace; appears as a two-word phrase in lines, not as a single token in the lexicon.
caveats: ਪਤਿਤ ਪਾਵਨ does NOT appear as a single compound word token in word_freq — it is a phrasal concept spanning two words (ਪਤਿਤ + ਪਾਵਨ/ਪਾਵਨੁ). Both component words are confirmed in the corpus. Search must target line-level collocations.

description: Worldly pride, arrogance, and ego-inflation (ਗਰਬੁ) arising from attachment to the transient world; closely related to ਹਉਮੈ (the ego-self, the 'I-am-ness'), ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ (self-conceit), ਅਹੰਕਾਰੁ (ego/arrogance), and ਮਦ/ਮਦੁ (intoxication of pride); the overcoming of ਗਰਬ/ਹਉਮੈ is a prerequisite for liberation.
caveats: ਹਉਮੈ (625 hits) is the philosophically deepest term — the fundamental ego-illusion that separates the soul from God — and could merit its own concept entry. ਮਦ/ਮਦੁ (73 combined hits) can mean wine/intoxication as well as the pride of worldly status — context-dependent. The cluster ਗਰਬ+ਹਉਮੈ+ਅਭਿਮਾਨ+ਅਹੰਕਾਰ forms a tight semantic field.

description: The paradox of dying-while-alive (ਜੀਵਤ ਮਰਣਾ): the spiritual death of the ego while the body lives, leading to true living in God; expressed in lines such as 'ਮਰਿ ਮਰਿ ਜੀਵੈ ਤਾ ਕਿਛੁ ਪਾਏ' and 'ਜੀਵਨ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਸੋ ਆਖੀਐ ਮਰਿ ਜੀਵੈ ਮਰੀਆ'; ਜੀਉ (1406 hits) is the life-breath/soul; ਦੇਹੁਰਾ (the body-temple) is associated with this theme.
caveats: ਜੀਉ (1406 hits) is pervasive and primarily means 'life/soul/dear one' — not exclusively the ਜੀਵਤ ਮਰਣਾ concept. The phrase ਜੀਵਤ ਮਰਣਾ is a two-word collocation (ਜੀਵਤ + ਮਰਣਾ/ਮਰੈ/ਮਰਹਿ), not a single token. ਮਰਿ (204 hits) carries double meaning: (1) dying-while-alive (positive, spiritual); (2) physical death. Inclusion of ਜੀਉ in the count significantly inflates hits; it is included here as the underlying concept-token but should be flagged in queries.
